name: OpenCut
description: OpenCut is an open-source video editor positioned as the CapCut alternative, built with a real timeline-based editing model rather than a toy UI. Files stay on-device, the project is MIT-licensed, and it has grown explosively as creators look for a free, local replacement for subscription video tools. The repo tracks the full editor experience — timeline, effects, exports — as a web-first application that also packages into desktop installers.
highlights: 82k+ stars — one of the fastest-growing open-source video editors
Real timeline-based editing as a free CapCut alternative
MIT licensed with files that never leave your device
Web-first app with desktop packaging for one-click installs
curatorNote: OpenCut was flagged in the weekly report as 'too big to be a hidden gem', but at this point it is the open-source answer to CapCut — and the gap it fills is real. Watching how a local-first MIT video editor scales past 80k stars tells you a lot about where creator tools are heading.
